How is Roman concrete still standing after two thousand years?
Look at the Pantheon in Rome.
Its dome was finished almost nineteen hundred years ago.
It's still the largest unreinforced concrete dome on Earth.
A lot of it starts cracking within fifty to a hundred years.
So what did the Romans know that we don't?
In 2023, scientists at MIT found the secret.
Tiny white lumps of lime, all through the concrete.
But when a crack forms and water seeps in, those lumps dissolve...
and harden again, filling the crack.
And Roman harbor walls are even crazier.
Seawater reacts with volcanic ash in the concrete and grows new crystals.
